author: PavelMakarchuk
body:
**Verdict: Question — no action needed.**

**(1) Threshold age.** Yes — for MFJ, `pensions` and `gssi` are split 50/50 when both spouses are on the same side of the eligibility age (both qualify or both don't); when they straddle it, the whole amount goes to the older spouse. The default gate is **55** (the lowest state threshold, CO), with per-state overrides for the pension field only: **GA 62** (§48-7-27 tiers) and **KY 0** (always 50/50, since KRS 141.019 is per-person with no age test). `gssi` always uses 55. Code: [`policyengine_runner.py` (`_PENSION_SPLIT_AGE_BY_STATE`)](https://github.com/PolicyEngine/policyengine-taxsim/blob/21a7e5b/policyengine_taxsim/runners/policyengine_runner.py#L225-L260).

**(2) NJ.** PE does not model the Three-Year Rule / General Rule — it has no contributions or expected-return inputs. It treats `pensions` as the already-taxable amount and applies only the Pension/Retirement Exclusion: age 62+/disabled, times the income-tiered fraction (100%/50%/25% by total income under N.J.S.A. 54A:6-10), capped at the filing-status maximum ([`nj_pension_retirement_exclusion`](https://github.com/PolicyEngine/policyengine-us/blob/84253b6afafb/policyengine_us/variables/gov/states/nj/tax/income/exclusions/nj_pension_retirement_exclusion.py), [`nj_retirement_exclusion_fraction`](https://github.com/PolicyEngine/policyengine-us/blob/84253b6afafb/policyengine_us/variables/gov/states/nj/tax/income/exclusions/nj_retirement_exclusion_fraction.py)). So the taxable-portion determination is an input assumption, same as TAXSIM's.
